subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: If y = x^n, what is dy/dx?
questions.explain: The power rule brings the power down as a multiplier and reduces it by one.

questions.q: At a stationary point on a curve, the value of dy/dx is:
questions.explain: A stationary point occurs where the gradient of the curve is zero.

questions.q: For an arithmetic sequence with first term a and common difference d, the nth term is:
questions.explain: The nth term adds (n - 1) lots of the common difference to the first term.

questions.q: For any non-zero value a, what is a^0?
questions.explain: By the laws of indices, any non-zero number raised to the power zero equals 1.

questions.q: If y is directly proportional to x, this can be written as:
questions.explain: Direct proportion means y equals a constant k multiplied by x.

questions.q: What does the notation f^-1(x) represent?
questions.explain: f^-1(x) denotes the inverse function, which reverses the effect of f.

questions.q: When you multiply or divide both sides of an inequality by a negative number, you must:
options: Keep the inequality sign the same
Change it to an equals sign
questions.explain: Multiplying or dividing by a negative reverses the direction of the inequality.

questions.q: Find the nth term of the sequence 3, 7, 11, 15, ...
questions.explain: The common difference is 4, and 4n - 1 gives the correct terms starting at 3.
